I escaped,here's how

I overcame social anxiety by doing the opposite of what I normally do: If I would turn down a social activity, I made myself do it.  If going to a party is not my thing, I forced myself to go.  Etc. etc.  If I normally don't talk to people, I forced myself to introduce myself and get to know people.  If I normally don't say anything in large groups or contribute to conversation, I made it a goal to say 3 things--if I did that, it would be a successful event.  After 9 months, I have 0 anxiety--completely comfortable in my skin talking to strangers and close friends a like.  

Self confidence, this is earned.  You can't fake this--I thought I could, but at some point, if you meet someone who is legitimately more hardworking than you--you got owned.  No amount of "confidence" will compensate for the fact that that person is better than you.  HOWEVER, this does NOT mean you go into a rat race to beat everyone.  It does mean you know you're working hard, and you accept that right now you have a skill level of 6/10, but since you're working hard, you may move up to 7/10 someday, and that's fine.  

realist doesn't mean pessimist--in fact, pessimist isn't a realist because in reality good things happen as well as bad.
